name: Chapter 12: Limits and Derivatives
description: Intuitive derivative, limits and their algebra, standard trigonometric limits, first principle, derivative rules and standard derivatives.

cards.term: What is calculus mainly about?
cards.definition: The study of how the value of a function changes as the point in its domain changes: rates of change (derivatives) and accumulation (integrals)

cards.term: Average velocity between t = t₁ and t = t₂?
cards.definition: \(\dfrac{s(t_2) - s(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}\): distance travelled ÷ time taken

cards.term: A body falls s = 4.9t² metres. Average velocity over the first 2 seconds?
cards.definition: s(2) = 19.6 m, so 19.6/2 = 9.8 m/s

cards.term: Same body: average velocity between t = 1 and t = 2?
cards.definition: (19.6 − 4.9)/1 = 14.7 m/s

cards.term: Table: average velocity from t₁ to 2 for t₁ = 1.5, 1.8, 1.9, 1.99: what do the values do?
cards.definition: 17.15, 18.62, 19.11, 19.551: increasing towards 19.6. From the right (t = 2.5, 2.1, 2.01): 22.05, 20.58, 19.649: decreasing towards 19.6

cards.term: Instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocities (secant to tangent)
cards.definition: Derivative = limit of secant slopes as h→0; for s=4.9t² at t=2 the average velocity 19.6+4.9h tends to 19.6 m/s = slope of the tangent

cards.term: Instantaneous velocity at t = 2 for s = 4.9t²?
cards.definition: 19.6 m/s (between 19.551 and 19.649 from the tables). It is the derivative s′(2) = the slope of the tangent at t = 2

cards.term: Why must the left and right sequences of average velocities meet at one value?
cards.definition: Physically the body has a single velocity at t = 2. Both sequences squeeze the same number, the limit of the average velocity as the interval → 0

cards.term: Explain lim x→a f(x) = l in words.
cards.definition: As x gets close to a (but ≠ a), f(x) gets close to l. l is the value f “should take” at a judging from nearby values

cards.term: Left-hand and right-hand limits?
cards.definition: LHL: lim x→a⁻ f(x) (values with x < a). RHL: lim x→a⁺ f(x) (x > a). The limit exists iff LHL = RHL (finite)

cards.term: Left and right limits differ: the limit does not exist
cards.definition: lim exists iff left and right limits are equal; step function 1 (x≤0), 2 (x>0) has LHL 1, RHL 2 at 0, so no limit though f(0)=1

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
One-sided limits

f(x) = 1 for x ≤ 0 and f(x) = 2 for x > 0. What are the left and right limits at 0? Does the limit exist?

Approach 0 from each side separately.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
One-sided limits

f(x) = 1 for x ≤ 0 and f(x) = 2 for x > 0. What are the left and right limits at 0? Does the limit exist?

Left-hand limit (x → 0⁻) = 1; right-hand limit (x → 0⁺) = 2. They differ, so lim x→0 f(x) does not exist, even though f(0) = 1 is defined.

Rule: the limit exists ⟺ left limit = right limit (both finite).

cards.term: Can the limit exist at a point where f is undefined? Can f(a) and the limit differ?
cards.definition: Yes to both. e.g. f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) has limit 4 at 2 but f(2) is undefined; a function can also be defined at a with f(a) ≠ limit

cards.term: Limit at a hole: (x²−4)/(x−2) → 4
cards.definition: lim x→2 (x²−4)/(x−2) = 4 after cancelling the common factor; graph is y=x+2 with a hole at (2,4); limit ignores the value at the point

cards.term: Illustration: f(x) = x² as x → 0; g(x) = |x| as x → 0?
cards.definition: 0 and 0 (g(0) is not needed)

cards.term: Illustration 1–3: lim x→5 (x + 10); lim x→1 x³; lim x→2 3x.
cards.definition: 15, 1, 6: for polynomials the limit equals the value at the point

cards.term: Limit of a constant function f(x) = c at any a?
cards.definition: c

cards.term: Illustration 5: lim x→1 (x² + x)?
cards.definition: 2 (substitute; polynomial)

cards.term: Illustration 6–7: lim x→π/2 sin x; lim x→0 (x + cos x).
cards.definition: 1 and 1

cards.term: Illustration 8: f(x) = 1/x² for x > 0 as x → 0. What happens?
cards.definition: f(x) grows without bound: lim = +∞ (the limit does not exist as a finite number; not needed further in this course)

cards.term: Illustration 9: f(x) = x − 2 for x < 0, 0 at x = 0, x + 2 for x > 0. lim at 0?
cards.definition: LHL = −2, RHL = +2 → does not exist (even though f(0) = 0 is defined)

cards.term: Illustration 10: f(x) = x + 2 for x ≠ 1 and f(1) = 3?
cards.definition: x + 2 → 3 at 1: lim = 3 (here it equals f(1); in general they may differ)

cards.term: Theorem 1: algebra of limits (both limits exist).
cards.definition: lim (f ± g) = lim f ± lim g lim (fg) = lim f · lim g lim (f/g) = lim f / lim g if lim g ≠ 0 lim (λf) = λ lim f

cards.term: Limit of a polynomial at a?
cards.definition: Just substitute:\[\lim x\to a p(x) = p(a)\]

cards.term: Limit of a rational function g/h at a when h(a) ≠ 0? When h(a) = 0?
cards.definition: h(a) ≠ 0: substitute, g(a)/h(a). h(a) = 0 and g(a) ≠ 0: limit does not exist (infinite). h(a) = 0 and g(a) = 0: cancel the common factor (x − a) and try again

cards.term: Indeterminate form: what is 0/0 and what do you do?
cards.definition: Substituting gives 0/0, which tells nothing. Factorise (or rationalise) and cancel the factor (x − a) that causes it (allowed because x ≠ a)

cards.term: Example 1: lim x→1 (x³ − x² + 1); lim x→3 (x(x + 1)); lim x→−1 (1 + x + x² + … + x¹⁰).
cards.definition: 1; 12; 1 (alternating 1 − 1 + 1 … eleven terms)

cards.term: Example 2: lim x→1 (x² + 1)/(x + 100).
cards.definition: 2/101 → 2/101

cards.term: Example 2: lim x→2 (x³ − 4x² + 4x)/(x² − 4)?
cards.definition: x(x − 2)²/((x − 2)(x + 2)) = x(x − 2)/(x + 2) → 0

cards.term: Example 2 (iii): lim x→2 (x³ − 4x² + 4x)/(x² − 5x + 6).
cards.definition: x(x − 2)²/((x − 2)(x − 3)) = x(x − 2)/(x − 3): as x → 2 this → 0. But lim x→3 has a zero denominator with non-zero numerator: does not exist

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q1–4: lim x→3 (x + 3); lim x→π (x − 22/7); lim r→1 πr²; lim x→4 (4x + 3)/(x − 2).
cards.definition: 6; π − 22/7; π; 19/2
−1/2; 5; (3x + 5)(x − 2)/((x − 2)(x + 2)) → 11/4
(x − 3)(x + 3)(x² + 9)/((x − 3)(2x + 1)) → 108/7; b
Put w = z^(1/6): (w² − 1)/(w − 1) = w + 1 → 2; 1; (2 + x)/(2x(x + 2)) → −1/4

cards.term: Theorem 2: lim x→a (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = ?
cards.definition: n · aⁿ⁻¹ (true for any rational n and a > 0). It is the derivative of xⁿ at a

cards.term: Proof idea of lim (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = n aⁿ⁻¹.
cards.definition:
xⁿ − aⁿ = (x − a)(xⁿ⁻¹ + xⁿ⁻²a + … + aⁿ⁻¹)
cancel (x − a)
substitute x = a: n terms each aⁿ⁻¹

cards.term: Example 3: lim x→1 (x¹⁵ − 1)/(x¹⁰ − 1) and lim x→0 (√(1 + x) − 1)/x.
cards.definition: 15/10 = 3/2; put y = 1 + x: (y^(1/2) − 1)/(y − 1) → 1/2

cards.term: Trick: lim x→a (xᵐ − aᵐ)/(xⁿ − aⁿ)?
cards.definition: (m/n) aᵐ⁻ⁿ: divide numerator and denominator by (x − a)

cards.term: Theorem 3: if f(x) ≤ g(x) near a and both limits exist?
cards.definition: lim f ≤ lim g (limits preserve non-strict inequalities; strict inequalities may become equalities)

cards.term: Sandwich (squeeze) theorem?
cards.definition: If f(x) ≤ g(x) ≤ h(x) and lim f = lim h = l, then lim g = l

cards.term: Key inequality for 0 < x < π/2?
cards.definition: cos x < sin x / x < 1, from sin x < x < tan x (unit-circle areas)

cards.term: Sandwich proof of lim sin x / x = 1
cards.definition: sin x < x < tan x gives cos x < sin x/x < 1; by the sandwich theorem lim x→0 sin x/x = 1 (radians); also lim tan x/x = 1 and lim (1−cos x)/x = 0

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
sin x / x · sandwich

In the unit circle compare CD = sin x, arc AC = x and AB = tan x. What follows for lim sin x / x?

Compare two triangles and a sector.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
sin x / x · sandwich

In the unit circle compare CD = sin x, arc AC = x and AB = tan x. What follows for lim sin x / x?

Area △OAC < sector OAC < △OAB ⇒ sin x < x < tan x (0 < x < π/2). Divide by sin x and invert: cos x < sin x / x < 1.

As x → 0, cos x → 1, so by the sandwich theorem lim sin x / x = 1 (x in radians!). Then lim (1 − cos x)/x = 0 and lim tan x / x = 1.

cards.term: Theorem 5: lim x→0 sin x / x and lim x→0 (1 − cos x)/x?
cards.definition: 1 (x in radians!) and 0

cards.term: Graph of sin x / x
cards.definition: sin x/x has a removable discontinuity at 0 with limit 1, is even, and decays to 0 as |x| grows (squeezed between ±1/|x|)

cards.term: Why must x be in radians in lim sin x / x = 1?
cards.definition:
The arc length equals the angle only when the angle is in radians (arc = radius × angle).
In degrees the limit would be π/180

cards.term: Proof of lim (1 − cos x)/x = 0.
Example 4: lim x→0 sin 4x / sin 2x and lim x→0 tan x / x.
cards.definition: (sin 4x/4x)(2x/sin 2x)·2 = 2; (sin x/x)(1/cos x) → 1

cards.term: Method: limits of the type sin(ax)/(bx).
cards.definition: Rewrite so the argument of sine equals the denominator: sin(ax)/(bx) = (a/b)·(sin ax/ax) → a/b

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q13–14: lim x→0 sin ax/bx; lim x→0 sin ax/sin bx (a, b ≠ 0).
cards.definition: a/b and a/b

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q15–16: lim x→π sin(π − x)/(π(π − x)); lim x→0 cos x/(π − x).
cards.definition: Put y = π − x: sin y/(πy) → 1/π; 1/π → 1/π

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q17–18: lim x→0 (cos 2x − 1)/(cos x − 1); lim x→0 (ax + x cos x)/(b sin x).
cards.definition: (−2 sin²x)/(−2 sin²(x/2)) → 4; (a + cos x)/(b · sin x/x) → (a + 1)/b

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q19–20: lim x→0 x sec x; lim x→0 (sin ax + bx)/(ax + sin bx) (a, b, a + b ≠ 0).
cards.definition: 0; divide by x: (a + b)/(a + b) = 1

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q21–22: lim x→0 (cosec x − cot x); lim x→π/2 tan 2x/(x − π/2).
cards.definition: (1 − cos x)/sin x → 0; put y = x − π/2: tan 2x = tan(2y + π) = tan 2y, so tan 2y / y → 2
At 1: LHL 0, RHL −2 → does not exist. |x|/x: LHL −1, RHL 1 → does not exist. Same for x/|x|. At 5: |5| − 5 = 0

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q28: f = a + bx (x < 1), 4 (x = 1), b − ax (x > 1), and lim f = f(1). Find a, b.
cards.definition: LHL a + b = 4 and RHL b − a = 4 → a = 0, b = 4

cards.term: Ex 12.1 Q23: f(x) = 2x + 3 (x ≤ 0), 3(x + 1) (x > 0). Find lim x→0 f and lim x→1 f.
cards.definition: At 0: LHL = 3, RHL = 3 → 3. At 1: 3(1 + 1) = 6

cards.term: Method: piecewise functions and limits.
cards.definition: At the break point compute the left limit from the left formula and the right limit from the right formula; compare. Away from the break point just substitute

cards.term: General rule (from the text) for evaluating lim f(x)/g(x) when f(a) = g(a) = 0?
cards.definition: Factor out the vanishing factor from both: f = (x − a)ᵏ f₁ and g = (x − a)ˡ g₁ (f₁(a), g₁(a) ≠ 0), cancel the common power, and substitute

cards.term: Limits at infinity: lim x→∞ (3x² + 2)/(x² + 5)?
cards.definition: Divide by the highest power: 3. Rule: degree top < bottom → 0; equal → ratio of leading coefficients; top > bottom → ±∞

cards.term: lim x→∞ (√(x² + x) − x)?
cards.definition: Rationalise: x/(√(x² + x) + x) → 1/2

cards.term: Indeterminate forms (list)?
cards.definition: 0/0, ∞/∞, 0·∞, ∞ − ∞, 1^∞, 0⁰, ∞⁰. Each needs rewriting; 1^∞ uses (1 + u)^(1/u) → e

cards.term: L’Hôpital’s rule (JEE, beyond the syllabus core)?
cards.definition: If f(a) = g(a) = 0 (or both ∞) and f′, g′ exist: lim f/g = lim f′/g′ (repeat if still 0/0). Faster than factorising for hard limits, but not allowed as a “proof” in board answers

cards.term: lim x→0 (1 − cos x)/x² = ?
cards.definition: 2 sin²(x/2)/x² = (1/2)(sin(x/2)/(x/2))² → 1/2

cards.term: lim x→0 (√(1 + x) − 1)/x by rationalising?
cards.definition: x/(x(√(1 + x) + 1)) → 1/2

cards.term: lim x→0 (tan x − sin x)/x³?
cards.definition: tan x (1 − cos x)/x³ → 1 · 1/2 = 1/2
Write (1 + 2x)^(1/x) = [(1 + 2x)^(1/(2x))]² → e²

cards.term: Definition of the derivative of f at a?
cards.definition: \(f^{\prime}(a) = \lim_{h 	o 0}\dfrac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}\), provided the limit exists

cards.term: Definition of the derivative function (first principle)?
cards.definition: \(f^{\prime}(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}\). Notations: f′(x), dy/dx, D f(x), (d/dx) f(x)

cards.term: Geometric meaning of f′(a)?
cards.definition: The slope of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)): the slope of the chord PQ tends to the slope of the tangent as Q → P

cards.term: f′(x) is the slope of the tangent: (x²)′ = 2x
cards.definition: Tangents to y=x² at x=−1,0,1,2 have slopes −2,0,2,4 = 2x; f′(x)=lim (f(x+h)−f(x))/h; (x²)′=2x

cards.term: Tangent line at (a, f(a))? Normal?
cards.definition: y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a); normal (⟂): y − f(a) = −(1/f′(a))(x − a)

cards.term: Example 5: derivative of 3x at x = 2.
cards.definition: lim (3(2 + h) − 6)/h = 3

cards.term: Example 6: f(x) = 2x² + 3x − 5. Find f′(−1) and prove f′(0) + 3f′(−1) = 0.
Example 7: derivative of sin x at 0?
cards.definition: lim sin h/h = 1 (= cos 0)

cards.term: Example 8 and 11: derivative of a constant function?
cards.definition: 0: f(x + h) − f(x) = 0 for every h

cards.term: Example 9: derivative of 10x from first principle.
cards.definition: lim (10(x + h) − 10x)/h = 10

cards.term: Example 10: derivative of x² from first principle.
cards.definition: lim ((x + h)² − x²)/h = lim (2x + h) = 2x

cards.term: Example 12: derivative of 1/x from first principle.
cards.definition: lim (1/(x + h) − 1/x)/h = lim (−1)/(x(x + h)) = −1/x²

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q1–3: derivative of x² − 2 at x = 10; of x at x = 1; of 99x at x = 100.
cards.definition: 20; 1; 99

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q4: first principle: x³ − 27; (x − 1)(x − 2); 1/x²; (x + 1)/(x − 1).
cards.definition: 3x²; 2x − 3; −2/x³; −2/(x − 1)²

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q10: derivative of cos x from first principle.
cards.definition: (cos(x + h) − cos x)/h = (−2 sin(x + h/2) sin(h/2))/h → −sin x

cards.term: Example 19: derivative of 1/(x − 2)... first principle (function undefined at 2).
cards.definition: −1/(x − 2)², undefined at x = 2 as well: the derivative exists only where the function is defined and smooth

cards.term: Trap: is f′(a) the same as (f(a))′?
cards.definition: No. (f(a))′ is the derivative of a constant = 0. f′(a) means: differentiate f first, then substitute a

cards.term: Rules of differentiation
cards.definition: Sum / difference: (u ± v)′ = u′ ± v′; Constant multiple: (cu)′ = c u′; Product (Leibnitz) rule: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′; Quotient rule: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v²; Power rule: (xⁿ)′ = n xⁿ⁻¹; Chain rule (beyond the text): (f(g(x)))′ = f′(g(x)) · g′(x)

cards.term: Memory aid for the quotient rule?
cards.definition: “low d-high minus high d-low, over low squared”: (u/v)′ = (v u′ − u v′)/v². The order in the numerator matters

cards.term: Theorem 6: derivative of xⁿ?
cards.definition: n xⁿ⁻¹. Proof: by the binomial theorem (x + h)ⁿ − xⁿ = h(nxⁿ⁻¹ + … + hⁿ⁻¹). True for every real n

cards.term: Derivative of a polynomial a₀ + a₁x + … + aₙxⁿ?
cards.definition: a₁ + 2a₂x + 3a₃x² + … + n aₙ xⁿ⁻¹

cards.definition: 600x⁹⁹ − 55x⁵⁴ + 1

cards.term: Example 14: derivative of 1 + x + x² + … + x⁵⁰ at x = 1.
cards.definition: 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 50 = 1275

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q9(i)–(iii): differentiate x − 3/4... use: (5x³ + 3x − 1)(x − 1) and x⁻³(5 + 3x).
cards.definition: Expand first: 5x⁴ − 5x³ + 3x² − 4x + 1 → 20x³ − 15x² + 6x − 4. x⁻³(5 + 3x) = 5x⁻³ + 3x⁻² → −15x⁻⁴ − 6x⁻³

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q9(iv)–(v): x⁵(3 − 6x⁻⁹) and x⁻⁴(3 − 4x⁻⁵).
cards.definition: 3x⁵ − 6x⁻⁴ → 15x⁴ + 24x⁻⁵; 3x⁻⁴ − 4x⁻⁹ → −12x⁻⁵ + 36x⁻¹⁰

cards.term: Ex 12.2 Q7: derivative of (x − a)(x − b); (ax² + b)²; (x − a)/(x − b).
cards.definition: 2x − a − b; 4ax(ax² + b); quotient rule: (a − b)/(x − b)²

cards.term: Example 15: derivative of (x + 1)/x.
cards.definition: u = x + 1, v = x: (x − (x + 1))/x² = −1/x²

cards.term: Product rule example: differentiate x² sin x.
cards.definition: 2x sin x + x² cos x

cards.term: Quotient rule example: differentiate x/(x² + 1).
cards.definition: ((x² + 1) − x · 2x)/(x² + 1)² = (1 − x²)/(x² + 1)²

cards.definition: sin x: cos x; cos x: −sin x; tan x: sec² x; cot x: −cosec² x; sec x: sec x tan x; cosec x: −cosec x cot x

cards.definition: v = ds/dt, a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². For s = 4.9t²: v = 9.8t, a = 9.8 = g

cards.definition: Increasing and decreasing (used heavily in Class 12 applications)

cards.term: Differentiability and continuity?
cards.definition:
Differentiable at a ⟹ continuous at a.
The converse is false: |x| is continuous at 0 but has no derivative there (LHD = −1, RHD = 1)

(a) cos 2x (b) sin 2x (c) −cos 2x (d) 2 cos x
cards.definition: (a): cos²x − sin²x

cards.term:
MCQ: The derivative of (x² + 1)/x is
(a) 1 + 1/x² (b) 1 − 1/x² (c) 2x (d) x − 1/x
cards.definition: x + 1/x → (b) 1 − 1/x²

cards.term:
MCQ: If f(x) = |x|, then lim x→0 f(x) and f′(0)?
(a) 0 and 0 (b) 0 and 1 (c) 0 and does not exist (d) 1 and 0
cards.definition: LHD = −1, RHD = 1 → (c)

cards.term: Integer answer (JEE Main): lim x→0 (sin 5x)/(sin 2x) × 2 =?
cards.definition: (5/2)·2 = 5

cards.term: Integer answer: if f(x) = x⁴ − 2x² + 1, find f′(1).
cards.definition: 4x³ − 4x at 1 = 0

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: lim x→0 sin x / x = 1.
R: cos x < sin x / x < 1 near 0 and cos x → 1.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not explain A (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a): sandwich theorem

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: If lim x→a f(x) exists then f is defined at a.
R: The limit depends only on the values of f near a, not at a.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true (c) A false, R true (d) Both false
cards.definition: (c)

cards.term: True/False: the derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.
cards.definition: False: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′

cards.term: 3-mark: differentiate f(x) = x² sin x from first principle? or by rule.
cards.definition: Product rule: 2x sin x + x² cos x

cards.term: 4-mark: find the equation of the tangent to y = x² at (2, 4).
cards.definition: f′(2) = 4: y − 4 = 4(x − 2) → 4x − y − 4 = 0

cards.term: Case-based: the height of a ball is h(t) = 20t − 5t² metres. Velocity at t = 1 and when is it at rest momentarily?
cards.definition: h′(t) = 20 − 10t: v(1) = 10 m/s; v = 0 at t = 2 s (the top of the flight)
